elements.quote: A living systematic review of the literature was designed, consulting the electronic online versions of the CINHAL, Cochrane Library, Cuiden, IBECS, JBI, LILACS, Medline PyscoDoc, PsycoINFO, Scopus, and Web of Science databases in November 2021.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a (living) systematic review.

elements.quote: The objective of this study is to identify the best available scientific evidence on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the mental health of out-of-hospital HPs in terms of stress, anxiety, depression, and self-efficacy.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective/review question explicitly.

elements.quote: Original research was selected, published in either English, Spanish, French, Italian, or Portuguese.
elements.reason: Only study design and language criteria are given; key eligibility criteria regarding population (out-of-hospital HPs), outcomes, and exclusions are not specified in the abstract.

elements.quote: consulting the electronic online versions of the CINHAL, Cochrane Library, Cuiden, IBECS, JBI, LILACS, Medline PyscoDoc, PsycoINFO, Scopus, and Web of Science databases in November 2021
elements.reason: Information sources are listed and the last search date (November 2021) is reported.
The abstract does not mention any risk of bias or methodological quality assessment methods.
The abstract does not describe how results were presented or synthesized (e.g., narrative synthesis).

elements.quote: In total, 2082 publications were identified, of which 16 were included in this review.
elements.reason: The number of included studies (16) is reported, but no total number of participants or summary of study characteristics is provided in the abstract.

elements.quote: The mental health of out-of-hospital HPs was affected. Being a woman or having direct contact with patients showing suspicious signs of COVID-19 or confirmed cases were the factors related to a greater risk of developing high levels of stress and anxiety; in the case of depressive symptoms, it was having a clinical history of illnesses that could weaken their defenses against infection.
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes results for the main outcomes (stress, anxiety, depression, coping).

elements.quote: Neither a meta-analysis nor a meta-synthesis could be conducted with the studies included in the review due to the high levels of observed heterogeneity
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted, so no summary estimate with CI applies.

elements.quote: Being a woman or having direct contact with patients showing suspicious signs of COVID-19 or confirmed cases were the factors related to a greater risk of developing high levels of stress and anxiety
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect (greater risk) for the compared factors/groups.
The abstract does not mention limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias or heterogeneity.

elements.quote: The mental health of out-of-hospital HPs was affected.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the findings regarding mental health impact and associated factors.
The abstract does not state the funding source for the review.
The abstract does not report registration name or number (PROSPERO CRD-42021259951 appears only in the Methods section, not the abstract).

The retrieved evidence contains no Introduction/rationale text describing the current state of knowledge or uncertainties motivating the review. The only mention of uncertainty appears in Results (text_4) regarding scarce EMS studies, which does not constitute a rationale section.
No retrieved evidence explains the importance of or need for conducting the review. The Methods (text_3) describe the protocol and research question but do not articulate why the review was needed.

The retrieved evidence does not mention any existing similar systematic reviews, nor any citation of a previous review being updated or replicated. Without the Introduction text, this cannot be confirmed as reported.

This is a review of the psychological impact of exposure to SARS-CoV-2 (an observational/exposure question), not a review of intervention effects, so no mechanism of action of an intervention needs describing.
The review examines associations between pandemic exposure and mental health outcomes, not a complex intervention or delivery context, so a logic model of intervention components is not applicable.

elements.quote: The search began with the formulation of the following research question by R.S.C., whose clinical response was possible, in PIO (Population-Intervention-Outcome) format [46]: 'Has the possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic (I) affected the mental health (O) of HPs providing health care outside the hospital (P)?
elements.reason: The review's objective/question is explicitly stated as a research question formulated in a structured framework (PIO), covering population, intervention/exposure, and outcome.

elements.quote: Has the possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic (I) affected the mental health (O) of HPs providing health care outside the hospital (P)?
elements.reason: This is a review of exposure effects (SARS-CoV-2 exposure) on mental health outcomes, not a review of intervention effects with planned comparisons; the authors appropriately used the PIO variant, so PICO comparisons do not apply.

elements.quote: The selected research studies had to meet the following inclusion criteria: (1) being original, (2) based on qualitative and/or quantitative methods, (3) with any methodological design, (4) submitted for peer-review, (5) published in English, Spanish, French, Italian or Portuguese, (6) completed after December 2019, (7) without geographic limitation, (8) with at least the abstract available, and (9) that in their results evaluated the impact of possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 on levels of stress, anxiety, depression and/or self-efficacy of the HPs who were working in public, private, or voluntary out-of-hospital EMS during the COVID-19 pandemic
elements.reason: Eligibility criteria are fully specified, linked to the PIO question framework, covering designs, setting (out-of-hospital EMS), outcomes, and population.

elements.quote: (1) being original, ... (4) submitted for peer-review, (5) published in English, Spanish, French, Italian or Portuguese, (6) completed after December 2019, ... (8) with at least the abstract available
elements.reason: Report characteristics are specified: publication status (original, peer-reviewed), language restrictions, date restriction (after December 2019), and availability of at least an abstract.

elements.quote: Opinion articles and editorials, studies of low scientific-technical quality, those that did not reply to the posed research question and/or were not in line with the objective of the review, as well as others that, despite including out-of-hospital HPs, contributed no specific data on this subgroup in their results were excluded.
elements.reason: The review does not distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported; exclusion criteria focus on format, quality, relevance, and lack of subgroup data.

elements.quote: Neither a meta-analysis nor a meta-synthesis could be conducted with the studies included in the review due to the high levels of observed heterogeneity between the participants, in the area of development, in the scales and measurement instruments used, and with the final results. ... Anarrative synthesis of the main characteristics and findings from those studies was performed
elements.reason: No groups used in the synthesis are specified or linked to comparisons in the objectives; only an unstructured narrative synthesis of study characteristics and findings is reported.

elements.quote: High methodological quality was established for the inclusion of studies in the review.
elements.reason: Notable restrictions (e.g., requiring high methodological quality, language limits, abstract availability) are stated without explicit rationales for these restrictions.

elements.quote: the electronic version of the following databases were consulted in November 2021
elements.reason: A single search date (November 2021) is given, but it is stated collectively for all databases rather than for each individual source, and no last-searched date is provided for the grey literature sources or other methods.

elements.quote: CINHAL (EBSCOhost, Ipswich, MA, USA), Cochrane Library, Cuiden, ... Medline (Pubmed, Bethesda, MD, USA), PsycINFO (Ovid, New York, NY, USA), Scopus (Elsevier, New York, NY, USA), and Web of Science-WOS (Elsevier, New York, NY, USA)
elements.reason: Database names and platforms/interfaces are reported (e.g., EBSCOhost, Ovid, PubMed, Elsevier), but coverage dates for each database are not reported.

elements.quote: The study protocol has previously been registered at the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews PROSPERO, supported by the Centre for Reviews and Dissemination of the University of York, under reference CRD-42021259951.
elements.reason: PROSPERO is named, but it is mentioned as protocol registration rather than as a searched study register, and no date restrictions for registers are reported; the PRISMA flow diagram mentions registers but no register search details or restrictions are given.

elements.quote: a manual inverse search strategy was proposed, reviewing webpages, sources of grey literature (ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global, and OpenGrey)
elements.reason: Websites and grey literature sources are mentioned generically ("webpages"), and grey literature sources are named, but no specific website names or URLs are reported.

elements.quote: In the face of any doubt or relevant data unavailable in the selected studies, we planned to contact the corresponding author directly, requesting the necessary clarifications.
elements.reason: Contacting authors was only planned for clarifying data from included studies, not for identifying studies; no organisations or manufacturers were contacted for study identification.

elements.quote: we planned to contact the corresponding author directly
elements.reason: No individuals were contacted for the purpose of identifying studies; author contact was only planned for clarifying data, so this requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: as well as bibliographic references cited in the selected studies
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies that reference lists of the selected (included) studies were examined for additional relevant works.

elements.quote: A total of seven new references were found when completing an inverse manual search.
elements.reason: Backward citation searching is mentioned (the inverse manual search and reference checking), and the flow diagram shows 'Citation searching (n = 5)', but no citation index/platform used or specific search date for the citation searching is reported.

elements.quote: the electronic version of the following databases were consulted in November 2021
elements.reason: No journals or conference proceedings were browsed directly as sources; searches were conducted via bibliographic databases, so this requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: Table 1. Search strategy adapted to each of the databases. | CINHAL | (MH 'prehospital emergency care' OR 'emergency care' ... | Cochrane Library | ... | Cuiden | ... | IBECS | ... | JBI | ...
elements.reason: Full search strings are reported for each database (CINHAL, Cochrane Library, Cuiden, IBECS, JBI, LILACS, Medline, PsycDoc, PsycINFO, Scopus, WoS) in Table 1 across chunks table_0, table_1, and table_2.

elements.quote: The selected research studies had to meet the following inclusion criteria: (1) being original ... (5) published in English, Spanish, French, Italian or Portuguese, (6) completed after December 2019, (7) without geographic limitation, (8) with at least the abstract available
elements.reason: Eligibility criteria (language, date) are described, but no explicit search filters or limits applied to the searches are reported or justified; the search strings in Table 1 contain no limits.

elements.quote: The initial search strategy was the same for all the databases consulted, adapting it to the particularities of each one of them (Table 1).
elements.reason: Adaptation across databases is mentioned, but no published search approaches, filters, or hedges are cited.
No natural-language processing or text-analysis tools for term identification are reported.
No tools for translating search strings between sources are reported; adaptation was done manually without naming a tool.
No validation of the search strategy (e.g., against a reference set) is described; only reproduction/verification by three researchers is mentioned, which is not search validation.

elements.quote: All the search strategies in use were developed, reproduced, and checked by three different researchers (R.S.C., R.M.C.G., and S.N.P.) for the purpose of guaranteeing the reliability of the results
elements.reason: Internal checking by three researchers is reported, but no formal peer review process or tool such as PRESS is described.

elements.quote: the following research question by R.S.C. ... in PIO (Population-Intervention-Outcome) format [46]
elements.reason: A PIO framework is mentioned, but the final conceptual structure and explorations used to develop the search are not described in detail.

elements.quote: Three independent reviewers (R.S.C., R.M.C.G., and S.N.P.) screened out possible relevant studies by titles and abstracts... The final selection of the studies, the evaluation of their methodological quality, and the data-extraction was completed in pairs (N.G.S.B.-H.O.B., J.J.J.A.-J.J.F.D., A.M.R.M.-M.M.O., and M.P.M.H.-A.M.S.)
elements.reason: The number of reviewers at title/abstract screening (three) and full-text/eligibility stage (pairs of two) is explicitly reported.

elements.quote: Three independent reviewers (R.S.C., R.M.C.G., and S.N.P.) screened out possible relevant studies by titles and abstracts... completed in pairs..., independently with blind reviews
elements.reason: Independence of reviewers is explicitly stated for both title/abstract screening and full-text selection/quality evaluation.

elements.quote: thereby resolving any possible discrepancies through consensus and, in its absence, calling for the participation of a third evaluator (R.M.C.G.)
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution via consensus with escalation to a third evaluator is described.

elements.quote: In the face of any doubt or relevant data unavailable in the selected studies, we planned to contact the corresponding author directly, requesting the necessary clarifications.
elements.reason: A plan to contact authors is reported, but the Results note 'At no time was it necessary to contact the authors of the studies' (text_4); only planned process described, no actual contact occurred, so reporting is partial.
No translation methods for non-English records are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No automation tools were used in the selection process; only Mendeley is mentioned for duplicate removal, which is reference management, not automated eligibility screening.
No externally derived classifiers are mentioned in the retrieved evidence.
No internally derived classifiers are mentioned in the retrieved evidence.
No machine-learning prioritisation tools or stopping rules for screening are reported.
No crowdsourcing platforms are mentioned in the retrieved evidence.
No previously screened datasets were used to eliminate records; records removed before screening were duplicates, reported in the flow diagram.

elements.quote: One group of reviewers (N.G.S.B., H.O.B., J.J.J.A., and J.F.F.D.) extracted data from the included studies using this form, whereas the second one (A.M.R.M., M.M.O, M.P.M.H., and A.M.S.) verified the extracted data.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers collecting data from each report is specified (four extractors plus four verifiers).

elements.quote: the data-extraction was completed in pairs (N.G.S.B.-H.O.B., J.J.J.A.-J.J.F.D., A.M.R.M.-M.M.O., and M.P.M.H.-A.M.S.), independently with blind reviews
elements.reason: Data extraction was performed independently with blind reviews.

elements.quote: thereby resolving any possible discrepancies through consensus and, in its absence, calling for the participation of a third evaluator (R.M.C.G.)
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution via consensus and a third evaluator is described.

elements.quote: In the face of any doubt or relevant data unavailable in the selected studies, we planned to contact the corresponding author directly, requesting the necessary clarifications.
elements.reason: Process for obtaining/confirming data from study investigators is described (planned contact with corresponding authors).
No automation tools for data collection are reported; manual extraction with a standardized form was used, so this conditional element does not apply.
No translation of articles for data collection is reported; inclusion was limited to English, Spanish, French, Italian, or Portuguese, and no translation process is described.
No extraction of data from figures or associated software is reported.
No decision rules for selecting data from multiple reports of the same study or resolving inconsistencies between reports are described.

elements.quote: the following data were specifically extracted from each selected article: title and principal author, country and year of publication, objective, type of study, place and period undertaken, size and characteristics of the sample, definition of variables under analysis and instruments used, principal results obtained, conclusions of the study and scientific-technical quality
elements.reason: Outcome domains (stress, anxiety, depression, and self-efficacy) are identified via the research question and inclusion criteria ('evaluated the impact of possible exposure to SARS-CoV-2 on levels of stress, anxiety, depression and/or self-efficacy'), but they are not formally listed and defined as outcome domains in a dedicated data items section.

No time frame of measurement for each outcome domain is specified in the methods; the results only note variable time points across included studies, which is not a prespecified specification of measurement time points.
The manuscript does not state whether all compatible results (all measures, time points, analyses) within each outcome domain were sought.
Since whether all compatible results were sought is not stated, no process for selecting which results to collect is described.
No changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance are reported in the retrieved evidence.
No changes to processes for selecting results within outcome domains are reported with rationales in the retrieved evidence.
The manuscript does not report which outcomes were considered most important for interpreting conclusions or a rationale for prioritisation.

elements.quote: the following data were specifically extracted from each selected article: title and principal author, country and year of publication, objective, type of study, place and period undertaken, size and characteristics of the sample, definition of variables under analysis and instruments used, principal results obtained, conclusions of the study and scientific-technical quality.
elements.reason: The methods explicitly list all data items sought via a standardized data-extraction form.

elements.quote: In the face of any doubt or relevant data unavailable in the selected studies, we planned to contact the corresponding author directly, requesting the necessary clarifications.
elements.reason: The authors describe contacting authors for missing data but do not describe any assumptions made about missing or unclear information.

elements.quote: A standardized data-extraction form was designed in accordance with the JBI [50] recommendations with the purpose of guaranteeing the homogeneity of researchers in the collection of the information
elements.reason: The data items to collect were determined based on JBI recommendations, which is cited.

elements.quote: Critical Appraisal Tools from JBI of the University of Adelaide (Australia) [47], considered adequate for the design of the study [48,49], were used to evaluate the scientifictechnical quality of the selected articles as well as to determine the extent to which the risk of bias was reduced or eliminated in their design, performance, and/or analysis.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly names the risk-of-bias/critical appraisal tool used: the JBI Critical Appraisal Tools (University of Adelaide), with references [47-49] indicating specific checklist versions for each study design.

elements.quote: Q1: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined? Q2: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail? Q3: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way? ... Q10: Do the conclusions drawn in the research report flow from the analysis or interpretation of the data?
elements.reason: The individual items/domains of the JBI checklists are fully enumerated in the text accompanying Tables 3 and 4: eight items for cross-sectional studies and ten items for qualitative studies.

elements.quote: Each individual study was classified as having a low-, moderate-, or high-risk level of bias based on the number of items answered with 'yes'. For qualitative studies (10 items), the methodological quality was considered low, moderate, or high if three or less, four to seven, or more than eight criteria were met, respectively [48]. For cross-sectional studies (8 items), the methodological quality was considered low, moderate, or high if two or less, moderate if three to five, and high if six to eight criteria were met, respectively [49].
elements.reason: An overall judgement (low/moderate/high risk of bias) was made and the explicit scoring rules/thresholds for deriving it are reported for each study design.

No adaptations or modifications to the JBI Critical Appraisal Tools are described anywhere in the retrieved evidence; the tools appear to be used as published, but no explicit statement confirms or denies adaptation.

elements.quote: Critical Appraisal Tools from JBI of the University of Adelaide (Australia) [47] ... were used to evaluate the scientifictechnical quality of the selected articles
elements.reason: The manuscript reports using existing, published JBI Critical Appraisal Tools; no newly developed risk-of-bias tool was created, so this conditional requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: The final selection of the studies, the evaluation of their methodological quality, and the data-extraction was completed in pairs (N.G.S.B.-H.O.B., J.J.J.A.-J.J.F.D., A.M.R.M.-M.M.O., and M.P.M.H.-A.M.S.), independently with blind reviews, thereby resolving any possible discrepancies through consensus and, in its absence, calling for the participation of a third evaluator (R.M.C.G.).
elements.reason: The number of reviewers (pairs, with a third evaluator available), their independent and blinded work, and the disagreement-resolution procedure (consensus, then third evaluator R.M.C.G.) are all reported; a pilot concordance test with eight reviewers is also described.

elements.quote: In the face of any doubt or relevant data unavailable in the selected studies, we planned to contact the corresponding author directly, requesting the necessary clarifications.
elements.reason: A process of contacting corresponding authors for clarifications is described, but it is framed generically for doubts or unavailable data rather than specifically for obtaining or confirming risk-of-bias information from study investigators; the Results (text_4) note it was never needed.

elements.quote: All the works that had initially been identified in each of the databases consulted were included in Mendeley ® Reference Manager (Elsevier, New York, US), with the objective of removing duplicates.
elements.reason: No automation tools were used for the risk-of-bias assessment itself; the only software mentioned (Mendeley) was used for reference management and duplicate removal, so this conditional requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: Neither a meta-analysis nor a meta-synthesis could be conducted with the studies included in the review due to the high levels of observed heterogeneity... A narrative synthesis of the main characteristics and findings from those studies was performed
elements.reason: The Methods do not specify effect measures for any outcome. The review used narrative synthesis only, and although odds ratios appear in reported study findings (e.g., text_4/table_4 reporting ORs with CIs), the authors never state which effect measure(s) were used in the synthesis or presentation of results for each outcome.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect sizes (e.g., small/medium/large effects) and no rationale for them are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Neither a meta-analysis nor a meta-synthesis could be conducted with the studies included in the review due to the high levels of observed heterogeneity between the participants, in the area of development, in the scales and measurement instruments used, and with the final results.
elements.reason: No quantitative synthesis was performed (narrative synthesis only due to heterogeneity), so there was no re-expression of synthesized results using another effect measure; this conditional item does not apply.
No justification for the choice of any effect measure is provided in the retrieved evidence; the Methods contain no discussion of effect measures at all.

elements.quote: The selected research studies had to meet the following inclusion criteria: (1) being original, (2) based on qualitative and/or quantitative methods... Opinion articles and editorials, studies of low scientific-technical quality, those that did not reply to the posed research question and/or were not in line with the objective of the review... were excluded.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes eligibility criteria and the study selection/appraisal process (inclusion/exclusion criteria, critical appraisal thresholds, screening by reviewers), and reports a single narrative synthesis ('A narrative synthesis of the main characteristics and findings from those studies was performed'). However, it does not explicitly describe a process for deciding which studies were eligible for each planned synthesis (e.g., tabulating study characteristics against planned synthesis groups); the meta-analysis was abandoned due to heterogeneity, and no group-based eligibility mapping for syntheses is reported.
